source_groups.label: Original Chapter LXXXV heading, 1642 polygon horoscope, composite war question
claims: heading
Chap LXXXV Rupert Essex
Chapter asks whether Prince Rupert will gain honor in the wars or defeat the Earl of Essex and what will happen to him.
Composite outcome is not one unambiguous yes/no question.
question
get honour by our Warres
One target is whether Rupert wins public military honor.
Honor is different from battlefield victory, survival or confinement.
question
worst the Earle of Essex
A different target asks whether Rupert will overcome the Earl of Essex.
Opponent's military success is a separate endpoint.
question
what should become of him
The final component asks about Rupert's future fate.
Contains imprisonment and personal survival claims not equivalent to military honor.
chart_timestamp
28 November 1642 9 23 AM
The original polygonal horoscope prints 28 November 1642, at 9:23 AM.
The old historical time/calendar has not been independently recast.
authorial_method
not under notion vulgar rules
Lilly says this particular question is not governed simply by standard vulgar rules.
Retrospective interpretive flexibility is a major test limitation.
authorial_method
particular Rules govern his Fancy
He argues the astrologer should use special judgment rather than mechanically follow Guido or Haly.
No prospectively frozen unique method or scoring weights.

authorial_process
at last came resolution
His later settled conclusion differs from the initial favorable social impression.
Both phases must be preserved; do not back-project final view as original instantaneous answer.
source_internal_forecast
gain no honour by this War

Subjectively broad prediction, not a measured battlefield endpoint.
condition

condition

source_internal_forecast
fall hatred and malice of all or many

historical_inference
own perverseness folly

source_internal_forecast

source_internal_forecast
should not be killed
